known.title: Data loss: Correct the promise that cleanup preserves every uncommitted file
Functional: Explain which model Antigravity uses

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 4
Raise: Data loss
Case: normal use - A developer runs `forge doctor --fix` while a finished worktree has an unstaged `uv.lock` change. The release note says the folder will never be removed, but `src/forge/task.py:962` excludes that lockfile from the preservation check, and `src/forge/doctor.py:191` restores it before removing the folder. The existing test at `tests/test_doctor_fix.py:275` confirms this behavior. The owner accepted the lockfile exception in `plans/FORGE-TIDYUP-1.read.md:129`; the new safety promise conceals that exception. State it in the release note so users know to save lockfile changes first.
findings.title: Data loss: Correct the promise that cleanup preserves every uncommitted file

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 2
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - A user follows the release note to use Gemini 4 Neon by setting `workers = "antigravity"`, but their Antigravity account defaults to another model. `src/forge/repo.py:597` sets Antigravity's model to `default`, and `src/forge/antigravity.py:454` selects a model only when one is explicitly configured. The existing test at `tests/test_antigravity_build.py:114` demonstrates a Plus account running Gemini 4 Argon instead. The note should state that the account default is used and explain how to select Neon, including its plan requirement.
